headline_marked: Shoe garland hung on [[Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman sculpture]] in Jhenaidah
headline: Shoe garland hung on Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman sculpture in Jhenaidah
summary: Unknown persons desecrated the monument of the 1971 war hero in the central bus terminal area, sparking widespread local anger.
details: Unknown people hung a garland of shoes on a sculpture of Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman in Jhenaidah, leading to widespread anger among locals.
Photos of the shoes draped over the under-construction sculpture at the central bus terminal area spread on social media on Tuesday morning.
The shoes were removed by midday, according to Kamaluzzaman, a leader of the district's Muktijoddha Sangsad.
Jhenaidah Sadar Police chief Md Asaduzzaman stated that police learned of the incident through Facebook and have launched an investigation.
District Commissioner Md Noman Hossain held a meeting in the evening and instructed police to take legal action against the perpetrators.
Bir Sreshtha Hamidur Rahman, born in Jhenaidah, was posthumously awarded Bangladesh's highest military honour for his sacrifice in the 1971 Liberation War.
He was killed on October 28, 1971, in combat against Pakistani forces in Kamalganj, Moulvibazar.

headline_marked: Govt [[considering dengue vaccination]] in long term, but not now
headline: Govt considering dengue vaccination in long term, but not now
summary: State Minister for Health MA Mohit says the government is thinking about vaccines to reduce death rates, but there are no immediate plans for approval.
details: State Minister for Health MA Mohit announced that the government is considering the introduction of dengue vaccines to reduce the mortality rate of the disease.
Speaking at an event at Holy Family Hospital in Dhaka on Tuesday, the minister stated that there are currently no immediate plans to approve a dengue vaccine.
The minister warned that dengue infections may reach their peak this month, urging the public to remain vigilant and take precautions.
He noted that the the Local Government Division is currently working to destroy Aedes mosquito larvae to prevent further spread.

During the event, Professor Farhad Halim Dono, a member of the BNP's standing committee, emphasized that improving the dengue situation cannot happen without controlling the Aedes mosquito population.
Minister Mohit also remarked that the health system cannot be improved simply by making grand statements to the media, but requires planned development.
caption:
Is a dengue vaccine coming to Bangladesh? The government is considering it for the long term, but not immediately.

State Minister for Health MA Mohit announced that the government is considering the introduction of dengue vaccines to reduce the mortality rate of the disease.

Speaking at an event at Holy Family Hospital in Dhaka on Tuesday, the minister stated that there are currently no immediate plans to approve a dengue vaccine.

The minister warned that dengue infections may reach their peak this month, urging the public to remain vigilant and take precautions.

He noted that the the Local Government Division is currently working to destroy Aedes mosquito larvae to prevent further spread.

During the event, Professor Farhad Halim Dono, a member of the BNP's standing committee, emphasized that improving the dengue situation cannot happen without controlling the Aedes mosquito population.

Minister Mohit also remarked that the health system cannot be improved simply by making grand statements to the media, but requires planned development.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com
